scope: world generation, lighting, palette native kernels and selected Java/JNI boundary paths
method: Read-only offline static source review; no application/native code executed, no network, no source modifications. Partial coverage explicitly enumerated.

hardening_candidates.title: Density grid dimension multiplication can overflow before bounds check
hardening_candidates.rootcause: Three positive jint dimensions are multiplied in signed 64-bit arithmetic. The product can overflow; Java performs the same multiplication. Native evaluate_grid writes nested dimension loops to the caller output buffer.
hardening_candidates.attacker: Only arbitrary in-process Java caller demonstrated; normal chunk generation owns the dimensions. NativeChunkNoiseSampler has no Java counterpart. No remote/player-controlled dimension path established.
hardening_candidates.impact: Out-of-bounds output writes and JVM crash possible with crafted direct API calls; not classified as a security finding across a trust boundary.
hardening_candidates.confidence: high on arithmetic defect; low on attacker reachability
hardening_candidates.counterevidence: Known production grid callers construct small fixed chunk/climate grids; plugins already have full process authority.
hardening_candidates.remediation: Use checked_count or division-based bounds against output length before multiplication; Java Math.multiplyExact with fallback. Apply to grid roots and each JNI dimension product.

hardening_candidates.title: Material batch length check multiplies count in jint
hardening_candidates.rootcause: count * 5 can overflow in both Java check and C++ signed arithmetic; later blockData indexing uses i * 5.
hardening_candidates.attacker: Direct in-process caller would need enormous count and output array. Surface generation supplies chunk-height arrays and bounded per-column samples.
hardening_candidates.impact: Potential out-of-bounds read with malformed API calls; no demonstrated remote exploit.
hardening_candidates.confidence: high on source issue; low on trust-boundary exploit
hardening_candidates.counterevidence: Production buffers are allocated from chunk.getHeight and filled through Java array indexing; malformed oversized dimensions do not come from a player packet in reviewed paths.
hardening_candidates.remediation: Validate count <= blockData.length / 5, or use checked_count before converting to index size; avoid signed index multiplication.

hardening_candidates.title: Beardifier dense bucket allocation is proportional to bounding-box area
hardening_candidates.rootcause: Full expanded structure bounds define a dense width*depth grid and resize two vector-of-vector arrays, with no cap or fallback before allocation; allocation occurs under noexcept.
hardening_candidates.attacker: A crafted imported world structure box is a plausible input; no direct player-controlled box route established. Upstream structure NBT decoding and box restrictions were unavailable for full verification.
hardening_candidates.impact: Potential excessive allocation/CPU and native termination; not promoted to confirmed vulnerability without external-data boundary verification.
hardening_candidates.confidence: high on allocation amplification; medium-low on import reachability
hardening_candidates.counterevidence: Ordinary generated structure pieces are small and selected near the target chunk. A world must first be installed/loaded by a privileged operator for the candidate import path.
hardening_candidates.remediation: Bound bucket count using checked widened arithmetic; if excessive leave buckets empty and use the existing linear candidate path. Restrict buckets to the affected chunk footprint or use sparse buckets. Avoid throwing allocation beneath noexcept without recoverable handling.

hardening_candidates.title: Cleaner-backed raw-handle sampler calls lack reachability fences
hardening_candidates.rootcause: Instance methods pass primitive handle to static native methods; the owner is not explicitly kept alive until native work completes, while Cleaner can free native state when owner becomes unreachable.
hardening_candidates.attacker: Normal last-use/GC timing is a lifecycle concern; no remote attacker influence over owner reclamation established.
hardening_candidates.impact: Potential use-after-free/JVM crash if owner becomes unreachable while static JNI is executing. No runtime reproduction performed.
hardening_candidates.confidence: medium; production lifetime anchors reduce exposure
hardening_candidates.counterevidence: Interpolated sampler strongly retains its three octave objects. Production density cache retains Java DensityFunction keys in thread-local arrays and LastCompile records during use; ordinary world noise state is long lived.
hardening_candidates.remediation: Wrap raw-handle native calls in try/finally with Reference.reachabilityFence(this), retain all child owners for composite arenas, and define synchronization/ownership for explicit close.

resolved_questions.question: Can packed storage values cause a native histogram or scalar/SIMD index overflow?
resolved_questions.conclusion: JNI enforces element bits 1..32, nonnegative indices, backing storage lengths, output windows and start+count overflow. Histogram increments only if value < histogram_size. SIMD loops split aligned middle and scalar tails. No malformed palette data exploit found in reviewed code.

resolved_questions.question: Can an arbitrary simplex permutation produce an out-of-range gradient table access?
resolved_questions.conclusion: No: permutation lookup masks input with 0xff and gradient selection narrows to uint8_t then modulo 12 or indexes a 256-entry modulo table. JNI checks at least 256 input ints.

resolved_questions.question: Do double/octave JNI constructors copy caller-owned data before release?
resolved_questions.conclusion: Yes. Checked 3*N/256*N lengths guard the flattened allocations, and successful constructors copy into owned arrays. Composite interpolated noise intentionally borrows child samplers; Java stores strong child references.

resolved_questions.question: Are raw JNI handle casts themselves a remote arbitrary-write vulnerability?
resolved_questions.conclusion: No remote source of raw handles was established. Handles are issued by native constructors and stored in Java wrappers. An in-process plugin able to forge raw pointers already has full process authority; missing handle validation alone is not reported as a security vulnerability.

resolved_questions.question: Are density caches obviously shared between worker threads?
resolved_questions.conclusion: Reviewed tryCompile paths compile and store results in thread-local ThreadCompileCache and LastCompile records. Cache keys strongly retain their DensityFunction. Global binding maps use a mutex. Concurrent cache rebinding/destruction remains a hardening concern only if cache ownership contract is violated; no production race proven.

resolved_questions.question: Do light levels index arbitrary queue buckets?
resolved_questions.conclusion: JNI caps levelCount to 1..253; propagator clamps candidate/committed levels and queue enqueue/remove check bucket bounds. Block-light rebuild checks matching column counts, shape flags and neighbor coverage before copying successful center output.

dead_code.classification: orphan JNI surface in repository production build
dead_code.evidence: No tracked NativeChunkNoiseSampler Java class/declarations; rg matches only this JNI file and comments. CMakeLists.txt:575-578 still compiles the JNI and facade. Native tests use the C++ facade.
dead_code.remediation: Remove the orphan JNI TU from production target if no supported external client is intended; keep test-used C++ facade or explicitly mark as prototype. Do not delete kernels solely due missing Java bindings.

dead_code.evidence: NativePaletteOps.java declares get/set/bulk methods only; no nativeCountUnique declaration or repository Java caller.
dead_code.remediation: Remove unused JNI export or implement documented Java API if required; preserve count_unique C++ tests if useful.

dead_code.evidence: Repository non-test symbol search finds declarations/definitions only; tests/test_block_light_engine.cpp uses it; CMakeLists.txt:400 compiles source into lattice. No JNI/Java binding found.
dead_code.remediation: Keep in native tests but omit production linkage until integrated, or document prototype status.

dead_code.remediation: Retain as tested C++ API only if intended, otherwise remove unused batch helper.

non_security_integration_observation.description: Patch creates native queue and runUpdates returns native apply result, but reviewed patch does not forward vanilla enqueues, and callbackPropagateLevel ignores nativePtr. May be obsolete/superseded integration defect; verify final applied source before reporting. JNI GlobalRef(self) has no observed normal teardown except disable/destroy. Not a confirmed vulnerability.
